generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a cushion plant of the high Andes, 3,200 to 5,200 m up, of thousands of tiny packed rosettes forming a bright green, rock-hard mound up to a metre or more high and several across, growing perhaps a centimetre and a half a year and living for centuries. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 0.42 m tall at 80 years and 0.55 m at 200. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: bright yellow-green rosettes.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 3 (about 1902), p. 63, as Laretia compacta (Phil.) Reiche: the plant builds conical mounds 1.5 m tall and more. The Chilean environment ministry's species sheet, as quoted in search results, gives cushions about 1 m tall and 1 to 2 m or more across; the project's photo notes (G3-LLARETA.md 1a) 1 to 1.4 m tall beside people. No upper limit is given, so height_max_m is left unset.

traits.woodiness.note: Kleier et al. 2015 (PeerJ 3:e843), as the project's notes G3-LLARETA.md and search results quote it (the page was not reachable here): dense, woody cushions; the notes' photo of a broken piece shows fine dark woody branching under a thin living shell. Overrides the family's 'usually herbaceous'; GWDD also lists a wood density for the genus.

traits.leaf_division.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: leaves light green, hairless, linear, three-angled toward the tip, sometimes resinous, undivided.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: leaves linear with no lobing mentioned; the ministry sheet (search results) calls them small and triangular. One horticultural site says finely crenate; not used.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63 and key p. 62: leaves 4 to 5 mm long on prismatic, very densely leafy branches; leaves of the outer branches less overlapping, longer and spreading almost flat. The ministry sheet, as quoted in search results, gives 3 to 6 mm (the low and high).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Chile's environment ministry species sheet (Reglamento de Clasificación de Especies), as quoted in search results (the PDF was blocked): leaves very small, resinous, triangular, about 3 to 6 mm long by 1 to 4 mm wide; old leaves stay inside the cushion.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: leaves linear, three-angled (triquetrous) toward the tip. The ministry sheet says triangular; a horticultural site says ovate.

traits.rosette.note: Ministry sheet as quoted in search results: rosettes at the shoot tips, each giving 1 to 5 flowers; the project notes (G3-LLARETA.md) agree: thousands of short shoots each ending in a small rosette.

traits.inflorescence.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: umbels terminal, on short peduncles; flowers 4 to 5 per umbel, on short pedicels. A simple umbel; overrides the family's compound one.

traits.flowering_position.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: umbels terminal, shortly stalked; Laretia's genus line says the flowers come out among the topmost leaves.

traits.inflorescence_bracts.note: Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: involucre of 4 to 5 thin (membranous) bracteoles; no length given. A horticultural site (search results) gives a short involucre of 5 to 7.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Counted: flowers in one (simple) umbel. Reiche (about 1902), p. 63: 4 to 5 flowers. The ministry sheet (search results) gives 1 to 5 flowers per rosette, the low.

traits.flower_colour.note: Ministry sheet as quoted in search results: flowers yellowish-green (amarillo-verdosas); the project's photo notes say cream-yellow. RGB for 'greenish yellow'. Reiche gives no colour for this species (yellow petals for its sister Laretia acaulis). Popular sites saying lavender or pink were not used.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Ministry sheet as quoted in search results: a dry, round schizocarp 4 to 5 mm, splitting in two one-seeded halves. Reiche (about 1902) says fruits large, fully ripe ones unknown, the halves sometimes unequal.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2667411), as no source read gives it.
